n982e6e4d7d55: In this autobiography, I describe my childhood and early education and summarize structural biology research in nucleic acids and proteins and my work with the Protein Data Bank.
ncea4acd33b2d: Over the past several decades, power electronic converters have become a key enabler of electrification across nearly all energy, mobility, and industrial sectors. Their widespread integration has driven significant gains in productivity and efficiency while fundamentally reshaping the dynamics of power grids and industrial processes. Modern power systems increasingly rely on converter-based technologies, which, due to their fast dynamics, reduce system inertia and consequently diminish inherent stability margins. At the same time, the transition toward renewable and distributed generation has introduced greater variability and uncertainty in the power supply. In parallel, industrial processes have evolved toward more modular and flexible architectures through their interface with power electronic converters. This transformation has led to enhanced controllability and responsiveness but also to increased system complexity and reduced robustness. This article explores the challenges and opportunities associated with operating power electronic converters in complex electric networks and industrial scenarios, with a particular focus on the role of automatic control in achieving optimal, reliable, and sustainable system performance.
n7f3c4ea9b936: The nonprofit hospital community benefit (CB) program has existed for more than six decades, dating back to 1956. The program has undergone several regulatory changes over the years to improve oversight, transparency, and accountability; the most recent changes were implemented through the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (ACA). As the 15-year anniversary of the ACA approaches, this article provides an in-depth review of the literature on how nonprofit hospitals have responded to ACA Section 9007 (“Additional Requirements for Charitable Hospitals”). This review summarizes the state of the evidence on CB activities specific to the ACA provisions as well as other related recent state policies, discusses CB spending, identifies gaps in the CB literature, and proposes a research agenda for the next 10 years to continue to build the evidence base on hospital CB activities. In addition to contributing to academic literature, this review provides a foundation for policymakers and practitioners as they consider additional reforms to the CB program to improve oversight, transparency, and accountability.
n969eeae3fe7d: by Hugo G. Castelán-Sánchez, Art F. Y. Poon Recombination is an important process in the evolution of RNA viruses. For viruses with segmented genomes, recombination can occur by reassortment of entire genomic segments. This process has played a significant role in the adaptation and spread of influenza viruses with novel genomic combinations, i.e., antigenic shifts. Reassortment is usually identified by discrepancies between the topologies of trees reconstructed from different genomic segments, e.g., subtree prune and regraft (SPR) rearrangements. However, this phylogenetic discordance can also result from errors in tree reconstruction due to insufficient information. The objective of this study was to evaluate the contribution of phylogenetic reconstruction error to the inference of reassortment events from influenza A virus (IAV) genomes from avian hosts. We curated a dataset of 11,795 complete avian H5Nx IAV genomes and sampled subsets of HA sequences with different expected levels of reconstruction error. Next, we simulated molecular evolution along the trees reconstructed from these HA samples, varying rates of evolution and sequence lengths to correspond to the other genomic segments. Because these simulations had no reassortment, any phylogenetic discordance identified from the resulting trees must be caused by reconstruction error. We found that simulations from random samples yielded about 32% as many SPRs as obtained from real data. This false positive rate was reduced to 4% when simulating trees from the most genetically divergent subset of HA sequences. By modifying the simulated trees with SPR rearrangements, we observed a false negative rate of 8.5%, which increased with the number of SPRs per tree. Overall, we found that reassortment can be substantially overestimated from phylogenetic discordance, underscoring the need to account for phylogenetic uncertainty and sampling design when analyzing IAV datasets for reassortment.
n9957dc7e8ac0: Background Postoperative delirium (POD) is a fluctuating confusional state occurring early after surgery. Given its fluctuating nature, POD detection is influenced by the frequency and timing of screening. Sparse assessments potentially underestimate the true incidence reported in individual studies, subsequently influencing the weight of studies in meta-analyses, and the results and precision of these meta-analyses. Objective To develop a method to evaluate the robustness of meta-analyses to the variation in the frequency and timing of POD assessment across included studies. Methods We developed an expert-based scoring system to rate studies according to the confidence that a patient reported not to have POD in the study truly did not, based on the reported timing and frequency of POD assessments. We describe how to use the system to generate hypothetical event rates for studies if the frequency and timing of POD assessment were optimal and how to use these rates in a sensitivity analysis of meta-analyses including these studies. We illustrate the method applying it to two meta-analyses as work examples, one of observational studies and one of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Results In our work examples, the expert-based score for the individual studies ranged from 33–77% for the observational and 22–70% for RCTs meta-analysis. Sensitivity analyses showed a change in the pooled effect size, heterogeneity, and precision compared to the original estimates. Conclusion We present a method to evaluate the robustness of a meta-analysis of studies having POD as an outcome, when there is variation across individual studies in the frequency and timing of POD assessment. The confidence score acts as a preliminary index of the robustness of meta-analyses. Through work examples, we showed that the robustness depends on the characteristics of individual studies included.
n67c22a2c10d1: Background Diabetic Neuropathy (DN) is a prevalent complication of diabetes linked to chronic inflammation. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and Interleukin-10 (IL-10) are key cytokines implicated in DN pathogenesis. This study investigates the association of IL6 and IL10 gene polymorphisms and serum levels with DN in the Bangladeshi population. Materials and methods A case-control study was conducted with 225 participants: diabetic patients with DN (n = 75), diabetic patients without DN (n = 75), and healthy controls (n = 75). Genomic DNA was extracted for genotyping IL-6 (rs1800796) and IL-10 (rs1800896) SNPs via PCR. Serum cytokine levels were measured using ELISA. Results Serum IL-6 levels were significantly higher in the DN group than in the other study groups (p < 0.0001), with the highest levels observed among individuals with the IL-6 rs1800796 CC genotype. In unadjusted analyses, the IL-6 CC genotype was associated with increased odds of DN compared with healthy controls (OR = 4.813, 95% CI: 1.752–13.85, p = 0.0040), as was the IL-10 GG genotype (OR = 2.679, 95% CI: 1.000–6.751, p = 0.0373). However, neither IL-6 nor IL-10 genotype remained independently associated with DN after multivariable adjustment. Serum IL-10 levels did not differ significantly among the study groups (p = 0.0948). Combined genotype analyses showed several nominal associations, although these findings were exploratory. Serum IL-6 showed promising discriminatory ability in distinguishing patients with DN from the other study groups, whereas IL-10 demonstrated limited discriminatory performance. Conclusion These findings support further investigation of serum IL-6 as a potential candidate biomarker for diabetic neuropathy, whereas the independent contribution of the investigated IL-6 and IL-10 polymorphisms remains uncertain. Larger prospective studies with independent external validation are required before clinical application can be considered.
n182af9794a4b: This study examines whether consumers’ willingness to pay (WTP) for ready-to-eat cereals differs between immersive virtual reality (IVR) and real-world (RW) environments. Real choice experiments were conducted with 227 respondents who selected reservation dates without knowing whether they corresponded to the IVR or RW setting. To derive consumers’ WTP, random parameter logit models were estimated primarily in WTP space, while preference-space models were used as a robustness check. The results show no significant differences in WTP between IVR and RW for any of the cereal products tested. This suggests that consumers’ product choices in IVR environments are based on monetary valuations, similar to those in real environments. When combined with real economic incentives, IVR-based choice experiments may therefore yield WTP estimates comparable to those obtained from conventional real choice experiments. To our knowledge, this is the first study to compare WTP between IVR and RW environments using an incentive-compatible experimental design.
n8a42ae64954c: Quantum neural networks learn by following gradients, and on real hardware those gradients are washed out by noise. Predicting how quickly this happens, before any finite noise experiment or circuit sweep is run, remains an open problem. We present CohAlign, an open source toolkit that computes the first order noise susceptibility of the ensemble second moment of a specified parameter gradient in a charge conserving brickwork quantum neural network. The computation needs only a classical description of the circuit, the noise model, the prepared state, the readout and the initialisation prior. The predicted quantity is distinct from training convergence or final accuracy. The key observation is that only the part of the noise that a measurement can actually see matters. A purposefully constructed control channel makes this clear, damaging the operator carrying a gradient at nearly the maximal rate while the measured gradient remains exactly as predicted and untouched. We validate the predictions against separately evaluated finite difference slopes across the benchmark suite, including a signed coherent case, in exact simulations at eight and ten qubits and on two circuit topologies.
n972dce73c098: Introduction Postoperative pain after cesarean section may delay recovery and impair function. Transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) and low-level laser photobiomodulation (PBM) are used for pain control, but the additional effect of combining these therapies remains unclear. This study investigated this effect. Methods A randomized clinical trial with four groups: combined TENS + low-level laser photobiomodulation (PBM), TENS alone, placebo, and control. Assessments were performed at 8–12 h (t1), 20–24 h (t2), and 44–48 h postpartum (t3). Outcomes included pain intensity, functional independence, functional capacity assessed by the Two-Minute Walk Test (2MWT), and cardiorespiratory variables. Two intervention sessions were applied after t1 and t2, except in the control group. Data were analyzed using mixed ANOVA and nonparametric equivalents when appropriate. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results A total of 88 women were included. Pain intensity decreased significantly over time in the combined TENS + PBM group (1.82 ± 1.18 at t2 vs 1.30 ± 0.86 at t3; p = 0.008) and in the TENS group (1.59 ± 1.05 at t2 vs 0.95 ± 1.05 at t3; p = 0.025). Functional independence increased in the combined therapy group (14.9 ± 3.3 at t1 vs 17.1 ± 3.6 at t3; p = 0.034) and in the TENS group (15.2 ± 3.0 at t1 vs 17.5 ± 3.4 at t3; p = 0.028). Functional capacity improved in all groups between t2 and t3 in the Two-Minute Walk Test (Control: 63.5 vs 76.8 m, p = 0.002; Placebo: 50.3 vs 63.9 m, p = 0.002; Combined: 48.3 vs 65.2 m, p = 0.0006; TENS: 61.1 vs 72.2 m, p = 0.005). No significant differences were observed between groups (p > 0.05). A significant time effect was found for pain (p < 0.05) and functional independence (p < 0.001). Conclusion Pain decreased and functional independence improved during the postoperative period. However, the combination of TENS and low-level laser photobiomodulation did not provide additional benefits compared with the other groups.
n378f05f25205: Deep-learning-based holographic reconstruction requires numerical data with reliable ground truth for training and quantitative evaluation. Experimental hologram acquisition and pixel-level phase annotation can be difficult to control, making physically defined numerical cases useful as reproducible benchmarks. Here, three analytically specified phase targets—a smooth Gaussian distribution, a four-level step distribution, and a radially structured Siemens Star—are used to generate off-axis digital holograms with known phase ground truth. A frequency-domain filtering procedure is applied before inverse Fourier reconstruction, followed by DCT-based global phase unwrapping. Reconstruction quality is quantified using root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), correlation coefficient, and profile-based error analysis. The results show that reconstruction errors are comparatively small in smooth regions and increase near abrupt or high-spatial-frequency phase transitions. The three cases are therefore presented as controlled benchmark examples for algorithm verification and baseline comparison, not as a complete substitute for experimental holographic datasets or as a complete training corpus for deep-learning models.
n0a03e162c363: by Melissa A. Hausburg, Kaysie L. Banton, Christopher D. Cassidy, Robert M. Madayag, Carlos H. Palacio, Jason S. Williams, Gregory W. Thomas, Raphael Bar-Or, David Bar-Or Systemic inflammatory response syndrome, driven by trauma or infection, involves excessive innate immune activation. Dexamethasone (DEX), a synthetic glucocorticoid, suppresses inflammation, although adverse side effects limit its clinical use. The inflammasome, a multiprotein complex that assembles in response to inflammatory stimuli like ATP after lipopolysaccharide (LPS) priming, facilitates caspase-1 cleavage and release of the proinflammatory cytokine, interleukin (IL)-1β. We investigated whether DEX and decanoic acid (DA), a saturated medium-chain fatty acid, inhibited caspase-1 activity and IL-1β release in an LPS/ATP-stimulated THP-1 macrophage model and whether co-treatment would allow for pharmacologic DEX dose-sparing in vitro. PMA-differentiated THP-1macrophages were primed with LPS overnight and stimulated with ATP for 3 h in the presence of DA, DEX, or both. Viability and cytotoxicity were assessed. Caspase-1 activity and IL-1β were quantified, and EC50 values were calculated by nonlinear regression. In control conditions, LPS/ATP stimulation induced 5.56 (q1: 3.51 – q3: 6.38) ng/mL of IL-1β release. DA and DEX inhibited IL-1β with full dose-response EC50 values of 131.7 μM and 24.29 nM, respectively. DA concentrations exceeding 800 μM decreased cell viability. An 8 x 9-point DA/DEX dose matrix (0–500 μM DA; 0 to 1e4 nM DEX) was used to interrogate drug interaction for IL-1β inhibition and caspase-1 activity. DEX EC50 values remained within a narrow 95% confidence interval of 17.5–26.6 nM, regardless of DA background concentration. DA reduced caspase-1 enzymatic activity with a calculated EC50 value of ~140 μM; whereas, DEX did not. These data show that DA and DEX act independently. Furthermore, compared to DEX alone, the presence of DA allowed for equivalent in vitro IL-1β suppression at lower DEX concentrations, supporting pharmacologic DEX dose-sparing. Determination of whether this pharmacologic effect translates to clinically meaningful corticosteroid dose reduction requires further study.
n75be20aa55f8: Surface electromyography (sEMG) has emerged as an impactful tool for controlling advanced prosthetic devices by detecting and recording muscle electrical activity during motion. This study presents a unique technique for recognizing nine distinct classes of finger movements by utilizing the Ninapro database. To address an underexplored domain of upper-limb prosthetic control, this research targets fine-resolution individual finger movements rather than the broad range of hand gestures. A custom-made one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D–CNN) was developed and validated using a within-subject evaluation strategy and signals. The proposed model achieved an overall classification accuracy of 90.1%. An in-depth sensitivity/specificity analysis for each finger movement class was administered to gain key insights into current recognition capabilities. The findings presented in this study demonstrate the viability of fine-resolution finger-movement recognition, offering foundational insights that may inform the future development and refinement of control systems in the prosthetic field.
n7aa47a7373fc: Background Excessive weight gain after kidney transplantation adversely affects patient and graft outcomes. Machine Learning has been increasingly used to improve risk prediction across a range of transplant-related outcomes, yet its application to post-transplant weight trajectories remains unexplored. This study is the first to evaluate the feasibility of using Machine Learning algorithms to identify predictors of weight gain after kidney transplantation. Methods This retrospective cohort study analyzed 374 adult kidney transplant recipients. We developed an Elastic Net regression model with 10-fold cross-validation to predict body weight variation at 12 months post-transplant. The analysis screened a comprehensive set of demographic and clinical variables, including recipient characteristics, donor type, dialysis duration, and pre-transplant hypertension, to identify predictors within the training (75%) and testing (25%) datasets. Results Mean weight gain was 4.0 ± 7.4 kg. The Elastic Net model retained four predictors in the final model: female sex, deceased donor source, age, and pre-transplant body mass index. However, the model demonstrated limited predictive performance (R2 = 0.10; Mean Absolute Error = 8.7%), indicating that baseline variables explain only a small fraction of the observed variability in weight change. Conclusions This pioneering study establishes an analytical benchmark and reveals the informational limits of standard clinical datasets for predicting post-transplant weight gain. While Machine Learning application is feasible, current demographic and clinical variables are insufficient for precise individual prediction. Future models must integrate more granular behavioral and pharmacological data to achieve clinically actionable risk stratification.
nc2d5c572d03e: by Kara M. Palamountain, Chethana Achar, Rebecca P. Kirby, Yukari C. Manabe, Debi Boeras, Michal Maimaran Introduction This study aimed to assess global stakeholder preferences for key attributes of point-of-care (POC) HIV Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests (NAAT), with the aim of informing product development to support progress toward UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets. Methods A web-based conjoint survey was conducted in August through November 2024 among HIV clinicians, laboratory professionals, and researchers. Participants were asked to evaluate hypothetical POC HIV NAAT profiles varying by six attributes: sensitivity / limit of detection (LOD), sample-collection method, turnaround time (TAT), result format, price, and power source. Relative importance and part-worth utilities were calculated to assess trade-offs in decision-making. Results One hundred three respondents from 33 countries, primarily in Africa (75%), completed the survey. The relative importance placed on the attributes in the conjoint task varied based on the setting. In community and home-based settings, participants prioritized fingerstick sample collection (25.90%) and faster TATs (28.8%), even at the expense of sensitivity (15.70%). By contrast, respondents from hospitals and health centers valued tests with high sensitivity (42.6%, 40.9%) and faster TATs (31.5%, 22.6%). Across all respondents, price (7.0%), result format (3.30%), and power source (7.25%) were less influential. Conclusions Stakeholders were willing to make trade-offs among desirable attributes, prioritizing rapid turnaround time, strong sensitivity, and fingerstick sampling over affordability, power requirements, and result format in the conjoint task. These preferences vary by level of care and by use case, underscoring the importance of aligning product features with contextual needs. Engaging stakeholders early in the design process is critical to ensure new POC HIV NAAT technologies are both acceptable and scalable in low-resource settings.
n00c756964349: Inflammation underlies numerous pathological conditions, driving the need for safe and effective anti-inflammatory agents. Anti-inflammatory peptides (AIPs) are promising therapeutics due to their specificity, efficacy, and safety. This study evaluated the cationic antimicrobial peptide IL15.3 for anti-inflammatory activity and cytocompatibility in vitro. IL15.3 demonstrated low cytotoxicity in MTT assays using RAW 264.7 macrophages, normal human dermal fibroblasts (NHDF), and HaCaT keratinocytes. In LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 cells, IL15.3 significantly reduced nitric oxide (NO) production and reactive oxygen species (ROS) in a dose-dependent manner without affecting cell viability. qRT-PCR analysis revealed significant suppression of iNOS, COX-2, TNF-α, and IL-6 mRNA expression, alongside downregulation of NF-κB, JNK, STAT1, and STAT3, and a reciprocal shift in Keap1/Nrf2 expression suggestive of possible antioxidant pathway activation. Label-free proteomic profiling identified 5,191 proteins, revealing a multi-modal mechanism of action. IL15.3 treatment exclusively induced 4 anti-inflammatory proteins (ISG15, PEX14, TNIP3, PR) and upregulated negative regulators NRG1, DAB2IP, IL-18BP and SOCS5. Critically, IL15.3 suppressed key pro-inflammatory mediators including IKKβ, JAK1, JAK3, JNK, and IL-1RAcP, demonstrating comprehensive modulation of NF-κB, JAK/STAT, and MAPK pathways. In silico molecular docking further predicted potential interactions of IL15.3 with iNOS and the Keap1 Kelch domain, offering preliminary structural insight consistent with its putative dual anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity. Together, these findings indicate that IL15.3 exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activity through multiple mechanisms in LPS-stimulated macrophages at transcriptional and proteomic levels. The coordinated upregulation of negative regulators and suppression of central inflammatory mediators collectively suggest that IL15.3 may represent a promising therapeutic candidate for inflammatory disorders.
n50b0a82de7bd: by Bradley A. Sheffield, Brian J. Cassel, Apostolos Perelas, Patricia Sime, Peter Jackson Purpose For ten years, nintedanib and pirfenidone have been the only approved therapies for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), with nintedanib subsequently also approved for progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF). Previous studies demonstrate low antifibrotic (AF) uptake, but differences by site-of-care and AF uptake after seminal trials (IPF: INPULSIS/ASCEND; PPF: INBUILD) are not well characterized. We evaluated temporal trends in IPF and PPF diagnosis and AF use at academic (AC) versus non-academic (NonAC) centers. Methods Using the U.S. TriNetX Collaborative Network, we compared IPF and PPF incidence, prevalence, and AF use by center type using linear regression across post-trial and post–FDA-approval windows (IPF: 2015–2017, 2015–2024; PPF: 2020–2022, 2020–2024). Slope differences (Δslope) were calculated as AC minus NonAC annual slopes; therefore, positive values indicate faster increases at ACs, whereas negative values indicate faster increases at NonACs. Results Across both periods, IPF prevalence increased more rapidly at NonACs, while AF use was higher at ACs (2024: 33.5% vs 20.1%, p p p p = 0.009). During the post-INBUILD period (2020–2022), AF initiation rose faster at ACs (Δ slope +1.42 percentage points/year, p = 0.002), while overall AF slope differences were not significant. Outcome patterns for IPF revealed higher mortality and lung transplant in ACs, but lower respiratory failure and oxygen use. PPF showed higher respiratory failure and mortality in ACs, and no significant differences in lung transplant or oxygen use. Conclusions AF use in IPF and PPF was higher and rose faster at ACs, suggesting faster AC adoption and potential barriers at NonACs. Mixed outcome findings suggest referral and severity bias may partially explain differences, however, are unlikely to fully account for them. More research is needed to account for referral and severity bias. Given the small NonAC PPF cohort (n = 216), PPF findings should be interpreted with caution.
n27cc9bfbb75b: Linear cultural heritage landscapes embody the long-term coupling relationships between ecological processes and human cultural practices, yet conservation models guided by a single ecological or cultural goal fail to meet their holistic management needs. Based on the perspective of biocultural diversity, this study takes the Huizhou-Hangzhou Ancient Trail (HHAT) as a case study and constructs a comprehensive conservation framework oriented toward spatial planning. Biodiversity and cultural diversity patterns are assessed and their spatial relationships are quantified using the coupling coordination degree model. The biocultural diversity index is further integrated with the Marxan systematic conservation planning model to identify Biocultural Core Protected Areas (BCCPA) and support differentiated spatial conservation strategies. The results indicate that biodiversity and cultural diversity along the HHAT exhibit a pronounced antagonistic coupling relationship: regions with antagonistic coupling account for 98.90% of the total study area, while coordinated regions make up only 0.02%. Based on the natural and cultural context of the study area, this pattern may be jointly influenced by rigid competition for small‑scale spatial resources, the dual effects of traffic corridors, and the cumulative effects of traditional livelihood activities. In response, an integrated conservation spatial pattern of one core area and two corridors is proposed, together with four conservation strategies: Conservation-Minimal Intervention, Conservation-Appropriate Revitalization, Restoration-Minimal Intervention, and Restoration-Appropriate Revitalization-enabling an effective translation from coupling diagnosis to spatial planning responses. This study advances understanding of biocultural interactions in mountainous linear heritage landscapes and provides a transferable methodological pathway for integrated conservation planning.
nc1c81893fccd: The main purpose of this study was to determine the differences in executive function performance levels of esports players who play First-Person Shooter (FPS) and Multiplayer Online Battle Arena (MOBA) game types compared to non-video game players (NVGPs). Other purposes of the study are to examine the relationships of executive function components and their relationships with in-game rank and total game play time variables. The study groups consisted of ninety volunteer participants, all of whom were male young adults between the ages of 18 and 34, 30 of whom actively played FPS video games, 30 of whom actively played MOBA video games, and 30 of whom NVGPs. Corsi Block-Tapping Test (CBT), Wisconsin (Berg) Card Sorting Test (WCST), and Stroop Test Çapa Form (ST) were used as data collection tools. According to the findings of the study; FPS players had significantly higher scores than NVGPs (p < 0.001, F = 8.55) in CBT and less error percentage than the NVGPs (p < 0.01, F = 5.58) and MOBA players had significantly less interference time than NVGPs in the ST (p < 0.001, F = 7.66). In addition, there was a significant negative correlation between CBT and ST interference times for all players (p < 0.05; r = −0.28) and a significant negative correlation between in-game skill and ST interference times for FPS players (p < 0.05; r = −0.41). These findings suggest that digital video game experience shapes cognitive profiles based on genre-specific demands; while FPS gameplay primarily enhances visuospatial working memory capacity, MOBA gameplay fosters stronger inhibition control, with higher in-game skill level reflecting superior inhibitory control in FPS gameplay, and relationship of visuospatial working memory and inhibition components demonstrating an underlying interrelated structure.
ncd9cafe28b03: by Vincent W. Klokman, Merel J. J. Verhagen, Adriaan A. J. Ros, Karlijn F. de Laat, Korné Jellema, Dominique P. V. de Kleijn, Kim E. Jie Background Patients with isolated acute-onset continuous dizziness (iAOCD) are commonly seen at the emergency department (ED). Distinguishing peripheral vestibular disorders from central causes remains challenging. Existing diagnostic tools, including bedside examination and neuroimaging, have important limitations. Otolin-1, an inner ear–specific glycoprotein, has been proposed as a biomarker of peripheral vestibular pathology. This study evaluated whether otolin-1 could serve as a diagnostic biomarker for this differentiation. Methods This study analyzed samples from a prospective multicenter cohort of adult patients who were seen at the ED with acute onset, continuous dizziness without focal neurological deficits. Patients were included within 24 hours of symptom onset. Otolin-1 plasma concentrations were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Final diagnoses (central versus peripheral) were determined by an expert panel based on clinical assessment, diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging and 3-month follow-up. Results We analyzed 245 patients (179 peripheral, 66 central). Median otolin-1 concentrations did not differ significantly between peripheral and central causes (517.6 [IQR 443.7–592.8] pg/mL vs 487.9 [424.9–644.4] pg/mL; p = 0.349). No significant differences were observed in hyperacute (<4.5 hours after symptom onset) or acute (4.5–24 hours after symptom onset) subgroups. Similarly, otolin-1 concentrations did not differ between central iAOCD and specific peripheral diagnoses. Substantial overlap in concentration ranges was observed across all comparisons. Receiver operating characteristic analysis similarly showed no useful discrimination (AUC 0.539, 95% CI 0.455–0.623). Conclusions Otolin-1 does not differentiate between central and peripheral causes of iAOCD in the ED setting. Although biologically linked to inner ear pathology, otolin-1 lacks sufficient discriminatory value as a stand-alone diagnostic biomarker.
n9294f09bf734: Introduction Syphilis has resurged across North America, including syphilis in pregnancy. Congenital syphilis can be prevented by timely treatment of syphilis in pregnancy, but conventional syphilis screening is problematic for people facing barriers to care. Syphilis point-of-care tests (POCT) have improved prenatal syphilis management in low- and middle-income countries. There is minimal literature regarding POCT feasibility and effectiveness for prenatal syphilis screening in high-income countries, where barriers and challenges may differ. Methods Academic and community partners co-designed a prospective single-arm feasibility trial to evaluate syphilis POCT implementation at a low-barrier prenatal clinic in Hamilton, Canada. The INSTI HIV/syphilis POCT was integrated into routine clinical care for pregnant people with ≥1 risk factor for syphilis (unstable housing in the past year; substance use or accessing addictions services in the past year; > 1 sexual partner in the past year; history of sexually transmitted or blood-borne infection; presentation to care >20 weeks gestation). Sexual partners of newly diagnosed pregnant people are also offered POCT. Individuals offered POCT are invited to enroll in the study. The primary feasibility outcome is the proportion of pregnant participants who accept POCT at first offer. Secondary feasibility outcomes include valid POCT results on clinician’s first attempt and accurate POCT interpretation by clinicians. Secondary clinical outcomes include time to treatment initiation and completion of treatment among syphilis-positive participants. To promote inclusion of groups facing structural barriers to research, individuals declining study participation are enrolled for limited prospective chart review (primary feasibility outcome only). Target enrollment is N = 62 pregnant participants over 18 months. Baseline participant characteristics and outcomes will be descriptively analyzed. Community-based knowledge mobilization is ongoing. Conclusion This pilot study will generate novel feasibility data regarding prenatal syphilis screening with POCT in high-income countries and inform design of a multicenter implementation trial. Trial registration Clinicaltrials.gov NCT06829602; February 17, 2025. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06829602
n63c50ff351d4: by Abdulmohsen Saud Albesher National digital health platforms are becoming fundamental components of modern healthcare delivery; however, patient experience is commonly assessed using overall ratings or sentiment analysis, providing limited understanding of the specific dimensions that influence digital healthcare quality and service improvement. This study aimed to develop a multidimensional framework for understanding patient experience in a national digital health platform, examine variation across healthcare services, investigate changes over time, and identify evidence-based improvement priorities. A qualitative analysis was conducted using 97,034 Google Play reviews of Sehhaty, the Saudi national digital health platform, posted between 2019 and 2026. Reviews were analyzed using an inductive coding approach to develop a patient experience framework, followed by comparative analyses across healthcare services and longitudinal analyses across successive stages of platform development. Nine patient experience dimensions were identified. Patient experience differed considerably across healthcare services, indicating that improvement priorities were service-specific rather than uniform across the platform. Longitudinal analyses showed a shift from predominantly technical concerns during early deployment toward challenges involving service accessibility, integration, continuity of care, as the platform matured. These findings enabled the identification of service-specific priorities for improving digital healthcare delivery. Patient experience in national digital health platforms is multidimensional, service-dependent, and evolves alongside platform maturity. The proposed framework extends approaches based primarily on ratings or sentiment by transforming large-scale patient-generated feedback into actionable evidence for healthcare quality improvement and continuous evaluation of patient-centered digital health services.
n4430eca20c39: by Kassaye Getaneh Arge Background In sub-Saharan Africa, child mortality remains a critical public health challenge, with Zambia exhibiting some of the highest rates in the region. While survival analysis has identified key risk factors, these methods often fail to capture complex non-linear interactions and the dynamic, time-varying nature of longitudinal markers like birth intervals. This study aimed to develop and compare predictive survival models to improve risk stratification for under-five mortality using the 2024 Zambia Demographic and Health Survey (ZDHS). Methods A cohort of 35,610 live births was initially identified, with a final analytic sample of 9,362 singleton births and 1,236 mortality events (13.2%) after applying exclusion criteria for maternal age and data completeness. We compared four modeling frameworks for predictive comparison: Cox Proportional Hazards (Cox PH), Lasso Cox regression, Random Survival Forests (RSF), and Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM), alongside a Bayesian Joint Model for inference on the birth interval and mortality association. The proportional hazards assumption was assessed using Schoenfeld residuals, and stratified Cox models were employed to address time-varying effects. Model performance was evaluated using nested cross-validation with mother-level outer folds and time-dependent Concordance Indices (C-index) and Area Under the Curve (AUC) metrics across a 48-month follow-up period. Results Under nested cross-validation, the four survival models demonstrated comparable predictive performance, with C-indices ranging from 0.745 (Cox PH) to 0.750 (Gradient Boosting Machine) and Integrated Brier Scores ranging from 0.095 to 0.096; pairwise comparisons across models were not statistically significant (DeLong’s test: all p > 0.05). The Bayesian Joint Model revealed a significant association between the longitudinal birth interval process and the hazard of death (α=0.035, 95% CI: 0.023–0.048, p < 0.001), supporting the maternal depletion hypothesis. Variable importance analysis identified birth interval and maternal age as the most influential predictors of child survival, followed by previous child deaths. Stratified analysis of the Cox model revealed significant effects for maternal education (Secondary: HR = 0.426, 95% CI: 0.318–0.570) and previous child deaths (HR = 1.648, 95% CI: 1.529–1.777). Conclusion Advanced survival modeling using joint modeling techniques provides deeper biological insights into child mortality dynamics, and machine learning and traditional survival models offered equivalent predictive discrimination and calibration in this analysis. These findings support targeted public health interventions focusing on birth spacing, maternal age, and enhanced monitoring for high-risk families as critical strategies for reducing under-five mortality in Zambia.
n1a4582afeff7: Background The tobacco epidemic is a global public health threat, with addiction often starting in the early adulthood stage of life. The Middle East Region is slow in adopting smoke-free campus policies, and few studies have examined smoking attitudes and behaviors among university students and their perspective on such policies. Objective The objective of this study was to determine the perceptions, knowledge, attitudes, and behaviors toward smoking (used to denote using any tobacco products) and smoke-free campus policies among university students aged between 17 and 30 years old at a large multicampus academic institution in Lebanon. Methods The study utilized a comprehensive cross-sectional study design. The questionnaire used in this study included validated tools for assessing smoking behaviors, such as the Global Adult Tobacco Survey (GATS); the Youth Tobacco Survey (YTS); and the Smoking Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices (KAP) survey, as well as sections for investigating attitudes toward smoking and the smoke-free campus policy. Results This study reports an alarming prevalence of smoking on campuses (32.2%), with more than half of the surveyed smokers reporting attempts to quit smoking in the past 12 months (53.4%). The factors significantly associated with smoking included having family (OR 7.08, 95% C.I (2.83–17.69) or friends (OR 12.20, 95% C.I (5.48–19.76)) who smoke, as well as experiencing social, emotional, or mental distress (OR 4.09, 95% C.I (1.74–9.63)). Further analysis revealed that agreement with a smoke-free university policy was a significant factor associated with reduced odds of smoking (OR 0.58 95% C.I (0.45–0.78)), whereas the perceived unfairness of smoking bans on campuses was associated with increased odds of smoking (OR 1.87, 95% C.I (1.34–2.61)). Conclusions The results highlight a promising window of opportunity to implement evidence-based interventions to support students in quitting smoking. Interventions include educational programs to raise awareness of the dangers of tobacco use and programs to break the association between exposure to stress and smoking. Such programs could include a combination of awareness programs and organizing stress-reducing services, workshops, and consultations. Because the design is cross-sectional, these findings describe associations rather than causal effects; they nonetheless support the further evaluation of smoke-free campus policies as one component of a broader strategy to lower students’ smoking rates, mitigate peer influence and foster healthier campus environments.
nf705e9324915: Background Adults with congenital heart disease (CHD) may experience substantial psychological distress. This study evaluated whether a documented history of anxiety disorders is associated with a distinct psychosocial profile in adults with CHD. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 45 adults with CHD were included: 21 with a documented history of anxiety disorders and 24 without. Psychosocial assessment included the EuroQol-5D-3L (EQ-5D-3L), Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES), State–Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI), and Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II). Associations between psychosocial measures and documented anxiety history were assessed using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for sex, NYHA functional class, and CHD complexity. Moderate depression was additionally assessed using univariable logistic regression. Results Mean age was 35 ± 9 years in participants with a documented history of anxiety disorders and 31 ± 11 years in those without (P = 0.230); males accounted for 33% and 62%, respectively (P = 0.052). NYHA functional class II–IV was more frequent among participants with a documented history of anxiety disorders (67% vs. 25%; P = 0.018). Compared with those without a documented anxiety history, participants with anxiety history reported greater limitations in usual activities (P = 0.021), higher anxiety/depression scores on the EQ-5D-3L (P = 0.023), poorer self-rated health (P = 0.038), higher trait anxiety (31.2 ± 5.8 vs. 26.5 ± 5.2; P = 0.008), and greater depressive symptom severity (BDI-II median 19 vs. 3; P = 0.001). Self-esteem was also higher (RSES median 27 vs. 25; P = 0.006). After adjustment, BDI-II scores were positively associated with a documented history of anxiety disorders (OR 1.14, 95% CI 1.05–1.28; P = 0.011), while EQ-5D VAS scores were inversely associated (OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.38–0.97; P = 0.048). STAI-State, STAI-Trait, and RSES scores were not significantly associated with anxiety history. None of the variables assessed in the univariable analysis was significantly associated with moderate depression. Conclusions In adults with CHD, a documented history of anxiety disorders was associated with greater depressive symptom severity and poorer self-rated health after adjustment for relevant clinical factors.
n56a115b718e3: Infrared object detection plays an important role in low-light and complex-environment perception. However, infrared images often exhibit low signal-to-noise ratio, weak target-background contrast, and limited texture information, which can degrade detection performance in small-target and cluttered-background scenarios while making it difficult to balance detection accuracy and model complexity. To address these challenges, this paper proposes TCLNet, a Thermal Contrast-Aware Lightweight Network for infrared object detection. TCLNet introduces a Thermal Contrast Encoder (TCE) to enhance local contrast-sensitive target representations and a Thermal-Guided Cross-Feature Attention (TGCA) mechanism to promote interactions between contrast-enhanced and semantic features, thereby improving target discrimination and suppressing background interference.Experiments were conducted independently on the M3FD, FLIR ADAS v2 (denoted as FLIR_2), and NUDT-SIRST1 datasets. TCLNet achieves mAP50 values of 60.5%, 45.4%, and 91.4%, respectively, corresponding to improvements of 12.8, 11.3, and 7.5 percentage points over the YOLO12n baseline. Meanwhile, the model maintains a compact size of approximately 2M parameters. These results demonstrate that TCLNet improves infrared target detection, particularly in low-SNR and small-target conditions, while achieving a favorable balance between detection accuracy and model complexity.
n7049596f5a17: The derivative is a fundamental concept in engineering education, as it enables students to model and interpret phenomena related to rates of change, optimization, and the analysis of physical processes. However, its teaching in higher education often emphasizes decontextualized algebraic procedures, with limited integration of authentic engineering problems and interactive digital technologies. This protocol outlines a scoping review aimed at mapping the available evidence on teaching and learning strategies for the derivative in undergraduate engineering education that incorporate authentic engineering problems, with or without the support of digital technologies. The review will follow the methodological framework proposed by the JBI Manual for Evidence Synthesis and the reporting guidelines of PRISMA-ScR. The review is guided by the PCC framework: (P) undergraduate engineering students; (C) didactic strategies for teaching and learning the derivative grounded in authentic engineering problems, with or without the support of digital technologies; and (C) higher education engineering programs. Searches will be conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, and SciELO for peer-reviewed publications published between 2000 and 2026 in English, Spanish, and Portuguese. Two reviewers will independently screen and select studies using Rayyan, and disagreements will be resolved by consensus. Data will be extracted using a pilot-tested data extraction form and synthesized through descriptive statistics, thematic categorization, and narrative synthesis. The review will provide a comprehensive mapping of didactic strategies, types of authentic problems, and reported learning difficulties related to the derivative in engineering education. The findings are expected to inform instructional design and support the development of evidence-based teaching practices in calculus courses for engineering students.
n8ca94fad7e3a: College athletes face substantial challenges from the combined demands of academic study and athletic training, placing them at elevated risk for academic burnout (AB). This study examined how perceived social support (PSS) is associated with AB by testing the mediating roles of mental toughness (MT) and athlete burnout (ATHB) and the moderating effect of cognitive reappraisal (CR). Using a cross-sectional design, 1,918 college athletes from over 20 Chinese universities completed standardized questionnaires assessing PSS, MT, ATHB, CR, and AB. Serial and moderated serial mediation were analyzed with the PROCESS macro (Models 6 and 89) while controlling for demographic and sport-related variables. PSS was directly and negatively associated with AB (β = −0.122, p < 0.001), with significant indirect associations separately through MT and ATHB and sequentially through MT and ATHB. CR showed path-specific moderation: at higher levels of CR, the negative PSS–AB association was stronger, but so was the positive ATHB–AB association, whereas the MT–AB association did not differ significantly across CR levels. Thus, CR should not be interpreted as having a uniformly buffering role. These findings may inform future multicomponent support approaches aimed at strengthening PSS and MT and identifying and addressing ATHB, while applying CR-related training cautiously and with attention to the specific pathway involved. The effectiveness and boundary conditions of such approaches require longitudinal or experimental testing.
nee883cb41904: Detecting small faces remains challenging due to scale variation and limited discriminative cues at low resolutions. We address this with a two-pronged approach. First, we modify YOLOv5 by adding extra convolutional layers and small-object–focused detection heads that operate on larger, higher-resolution backbone feature maps, improving sensitivity to tiny targets. Second, we introduce a dynamic, image adaptive patching strategy for scale selection. We compute Cr channel color probability maps and measure the number and density of pixel clusters; a Fuzzy Inference System (FIS) uses these cues to select the most suitable patch size for near and far faces. On the WIDER FACE benchmark, our method attains 93.07% mAP@50 (Easy), 91.25% mAP@50 (Medium), and 84.45% mAP@50 (Hard). On our proposed local dataset, the proposed model achieves 49.36% mAP@50 for different size faces. Beyond faces, the approach generalizes to small object detection on VisDrone-DET2019, reaching 46.76 mAP@50. These results demonstrate that coupling small-object-aware architecture design with color-guided, fuzzy patch selection yields competitive mAP@50 for small and distant targets.
n17874f8e9c9d: The steroid hormone dafachronic acid may carry the effects of reduced mTOR activity between tissues to coordinate metabolism and longevity across the body.
n601bcd0527b0: During locomotion, the coordinated activity of dozens of muscles shapes the kinematic features of each stride, including systematic changes in limb movement across walking speed. Motor units, each of which consists of a single motor neuron and the muscle fibers it innervates, contribute to the total activation of each muscle through their recruitment and firing rate when active. However, it remains unknown how the nervous system controls locomotor speed by changing the firing of individual motor units. To address this, we combined quantitative behavioral analysis of mouse locomotion with single motor unit recordings from the lateral and long heads of the triceps brachii, which drive monoarticular extension of the elbow and biarticular movements of the elbow and shoulder, respectively. In contrast to prior studies employing bulk electromyography (EMG) to examine muscle activity, our recordings revealed the diversity of spike patterning across motor units, as well as systematic differences in motor unit activity across muscles and locomotor speeds. First, motor unit activity differed significantly across the lateral and long heads, suggesting differential control of these two closely apposed elbow extensor muscles. Second, we found that individual units were recruited probabilistically (during only a subset of strides), showing that the highly repeatable bulk EMG signals observed across strides, in fact, reflect varying subsets of individual motor units. Finally, although recruitment probability and firing rate both increased at faster walking speeds, increases in recruitment were proportionally larger than rate changes, and recruitment of individual units accompanied changes in limb kinematics. Together, these results reveal how the firing of individual motor units varies systematically across muscles and walking speeds to produce flexible locomotor behavior.
n52da83b80ad0: Olfactory-driven behaviors are essential for animal survival, but mechanisms for decoding olfactory inputs remain poorly understood. We have used whole-network Ca2+ imaging to study olfactory coding in Caenorhabditis elegans. We show that the odorant 1-octanol is encoded combinatorially in the periphery as both an attractant and a repellent. These inputs are integrated centrally, and their relative strengths determine the sensitivity and valence of the behavioral response through modulation of locomotory reversals and speed. The balance of these pathways also dictates the activity of the locomotory command interneurons, which control locomotory reversals. This balance serves as a regulatory node for response modulation, allowing C. elegans to weigh opportunities and hazards in its environment when formulating behavioral responses. Thus, an odorant can be encoded simultaneously as inputs of opposite valence, focusing attention on the integration of these inputs in determining perception, response, and plasticity.
n6808a24d9bca: As elsewhere in the world, archaeological records in eastern Africa show that long environmental variabilities shaped the emergence and development of farming economies. Marine sediments and isotopic data indicate alternating humid and arid phases that coincide with the reorganization of settlements, establishment of agricultural landscapes, and the generation of new subsistence practices during the later Holocene. Strengthened monsoons during the African Humid Period (13,050–3050 BCE) produced environments that enabled human mobility, likely experimentation with plants, and the dispersal of early herders through the Rift Valley and the Horn of Africa. Archaeological, archaeobotanical, isotopic, and other data from sites in the Rift Valley, Lake Victoria, and elsewhere indicate varied and gradual transitions from foraging to mixed farming, shaped by microenvironments, altitude, and intercommunity exchanges. Case studies of farming systems developed over the last 2,000 years demonstrate innovative forms of resilient landscape engineering and complex social management. We suggest that the equity and collective stewardship attested by this record offer valuable analogues for contemporary climate adaptation in the Anthropocene.
n1ac9129e894b: This reflection on my years in linguistic anthropology also includes the broader sociohistorical transformations of which I have been a part. The Cold War and its aftermath were the backdrop against which we learned and taught. As a child migrant to the United States from the Soviet region, I became fascinated by the intersection of political relationships and linguistic practices. At the same time, linguistic anthropology was starting to navigate between theories of political economy and the analysis of speaking as action-in-events. Within that endeavor, I have studied conceptual questions about multilingualism and the workings of language ideology as well as questions about sign phenomena in constructing gender, sociocultural differentiation, scaling, and translation. My scholarly path has depended on the generous, inspiring influence of mentors, colleagues, and students, individually and in the many seminars and study groups we have formed together. Working now on analyzing authoritarian regimes, I see with alarm their effects on public expression, safety, and protest, echoing my earliest memories of repression.
nc37ea52f64d4: How anthropologists have invoked and conceptualized anxiety reflects the development of new ways of relating selfhood, subjectivity, and the sociopolitical to each other. This article examines the recent development of anthropological frameworks of anxiety in the context of the rising prevalence of and interest in anxiety. Since its inception in modern social theory, anxiety has functioned as a commentary on people's relation to risk, precarity, and emerging forms of capitalism. Early anthropological approaches to anxiety relied extensively on psychological theories that focused on the emotions at an individual level. Although they framed anxiety as a social condition in addition to an inner one, they were still beholden to the politics and ethics of the sovereign subject and dichotomies between self and society, individual and collective, and citizen and state. By framing anxiety as a social practice and relation, contemporary anthropologists are now redefining anxiety's role in political-economic transformations from a passive reflection of widespread uncertainty and insecurity to an agentive constituent of politics itself.
nb7d681096d2b: A review of the anthropological literature motivates an expansive definition of the therapeutic as practices that have or are purported to have salubrious effects on at least one of the parties involved. Those effects could be on the psychic or spiritual state of participants (i.e., what one is or has), on how they make sense of their state or circumstances (i.e., how one sees, feels, understands, or knows), and/or on their behavior (i.e., what one does and says, how, and to what effect). The idea that the therapeutic is invariably a matter of communicative practice is a premise of this review, which addresses ( a ) the diversity and distinctiveness of therapies as multimodal genres; ( b ) the therapeutic distillation of cultural values, projects, and ideals; ( c ) the epistemic and interpretive challenges of therapeutic communication, particularly relative to politically loaded questions of mediation; and ( d ) the scaling of the therapeutic as a kind of communication by way of communication.
n86ff13de8d4a: This article provides an overview of experimental anthropology, arguing that, from its inception, anthropology has operated as a form of experimental inquiry aimed at producing a surplus of data, relations, and sensations. We explore this notion through a tripartite heuristic for understanding how anthropological creativity draws on methods from the natural sciences as well as from art and design: ( a ) experience-based experimentation, ( b ) the adoption of scientific protocols and instruments, and ( c ) experimentation with and through models. Despite the apparent diversity of contemporary approaches, efforts to reimagine experimentalism in anthropology can still be understood through this heuristic. We revisit it in reverse order, arguing, first, that modeling now takes place through prototypes, games, devices, and other relational infrastructures; second, that apparatus-based experimentation has opened new possibilities for sensory enrichment; and finally, that anthropological practice itself emerges as a radical venture that expands conceptual, physical, and existential boundaries, with ethnographic inquiry relentlessly generating excess data.
n727fc55c624a: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct access to physical interactions at the contact interface, making it a critical modality for robust and dexterous manipulation. Over the past several decades, tactile-based manipulation research has evolved from mechanics-driven approaches, which explicitly interpret tactile signals through contact mechanics and task-specific reasoning, to data-driven approaches that learn tactile representations and manipulation policies directly from data. This article reviews the development of tactile-based manipulation from these two complementary perspectives. We first introduce the fundamentals of tactile sensing and then review, from a mechanics-driven perspective, how those signals form manipulation-relevant state representations and subsequently influence the robot action. We then examine the recent advances in data-driven tactile manipulation, covering imitation learning, reinforcement learning, vision–language–action models, and predictive models. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future opportunities toward scalable, generalizable, and robust tactile-enabled robotic systems.
ncfa127a7cc72: Forest insects worldwide face changing environments within a given year and across multiple years. Therefore, insects must match their life cycles with critical resources to maximize fitness and survival. A key strategy for life-cycle synchronization is entry into a special form of dormancy, called diapause. Diapause affects multiple life-history traits, including development, reproduction, movement, stress resistance, and energy storage. This review provides an overview and discussion of diapause expression for forest insects, focusing on ecologically and economically relevant plant-feeding species and highlighting specific, diapause-related features of forests. Diapause regulation and expression are highly variable across species and mainly help overcome unfavorable periods, synchronize life cycles with host trees and predators, and respond to scarce or irregular resources. Changing climatic conditions have direct and indirect effects on forest insect diapause, including temperature stress, energetic stress, and phenological mismatches. Knowledge of diapause regulation is essential for practical forestry to coordinate and evaluate management measures.
n263ea53659a4: In brood-site pollination mutualisms (BSPMs), insect pollinators breed within the plants that they pollinate. Organisms involved in BSPMs show adaptations in life-history strategies and life cycles. BSPM plants are monoecious or dioecious, or have bisexual flowers; are monocot or dicot; and are angiosperms or gymnosperms. All plants are perennial, mostly iteroparous, while a few are semelparous. The highly specific pollinators are mostly small-sized wasps, micromoths, thrips, fungus gnats, flower weevils, beetles, and gall midges. Most BSPMs involve ovule/seed parasites, while larvae also consume pollen, other floral tissues, and fungi. Active pollination occurs only in ovule/seed parasites, accompanied by special pollen-deposition structures and reduced pollen:ovule ratios. Quiescent stages involving egg, larval, prepupal, and pupal diapause enable synchrony with plant reproduction. Prolonged flower longevity enables the completion of larval growth. Haplodiploidy via arrhenotoky or paternal genome elimination often occurs. Many brood sites constitute mating arenas and impose restriction of mating opportunities.
nddc746c4812f: Candida ( Candidozyma ) auris is a pathogenic fungus first identified in a patient in 2009. Prior to this clinical finding, C. auris was unknown, with its closest relative being the marine-dwelling Candida haemulonii. Infections are increasing annually, predominately impacting hospital patients due to durable biofilms on medical devices and antimicrobial resistance. Perplexingly, the fungus arose nearly simultaneously across the globe in independent disease emergences from six genetically distinct clades. The C. auris clades mostly diverged from one another 5,000–10,000 years ago, during a period when global temperatures and sea levels rose and coastal wetlands flourished. Within the past 200–300 years, a new wave of rapid divergence occurred within each clade. This corresponds to industrialization, urbanization, global warming, and the widespread wetland destruction. Environmental stressors, including heat, are hypothesized to have driven mutations and stress resistance. These may not only help C. auris withstand a changing climate but also help it thrive within mammalian hosts.
nc2e699c45070: Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is caused by CGG repeat expansion in FMR1 , leading to gene silencing and loss of fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein (FMRP). As the most common inherited cause of intellectual disability and a leading monogenic cause of autism spectrum disorder, FXS has provided an unusually tractable framework for linking a single-gene defect to abnormalities in RNA regulation, synaptic development, circuit function, and behavior. In this review, we synthesize current understanding of FMRP function, dysregulated signaling pathways, synaptic and network phenotypes, and emerging contributions from glial and human organoid models. We also evaluate therapeutic efforts, emphasizing lessons from failed targeted trials, the constraints imposed by critical developmental periods, and newer strategies aimed at restoring FMR1 itself. We argue that future progress will depend on earlier intervention, biologically informed patient stratification, and objective measures of target engagement and circuit response.
n4e194ecc00f6: Dinosaurs dominated terrestrial ecosystems for more than 160 million years under fluctuating atmospheric conditions that profoundly shaped their cardiovascular physiology. Evidence from phylogenetic bracketing, fossil morphology, and comparative models with crocodilians, birds, and mammals suggests that many dinosaurs possessed a fully separated four-chambered heart capable of sustaining high systemic pressures and efficient oxygen (O 2 ) transport. In sauropods, extreme vertical distances between the heart and brain required arterial pressures exceeding those of any extant vertebrate, raising questions about cardiac structure, ventricular wall stress, and vascular adaptations. Oxygen transport was further modulated by atmospheric O 2 variability across the Mesozoic and therefore sauropods likely managed these changes by shaping their hemoglobin affinity, capillary density, respiratory system, and Bohr and Haldane effects. Mitochondrial density, redox balance, and the regulation of reactive species such as nitric oxide and hydrogen sulfide may have already underpinned thermoregulation, metabolic reprogramming, and tissue energetics. By integrating paleophysiology with modern comparative physiology, this review discusses how informed speculations on sauropods cardiovascular biology may be used to improve our understanding of endothermy, gigantism, and adaptive strategies in variations of O 2 /carbon dioxide environments. We posit that the necessary adaptations of the heart, microcirculation, and pressure–volume relations are relevant for understanding extreme physiology and, in some cases, human cardiovascular disease. This review synthesizes current knowledge on sauropods cardiovascular physiology, focusing on cardiac function, vascular architecture, O 2 transport, and whole-organism integration.
ne2e3bf4ba4c6: Cellular senescence is a stress-responsive cell fate characterized by stable growth arrest and acquisition of a proinflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype. Senescent cells accumulate with advancing age and contribute to dysfunction and disease across multiple organ systems. In skeletal muscle (SkM), emerging evidence indicates that senescence arises across diverse cell populations that collectively reshape the SkM niche. Through the SASP and altered intercellular signaling, senescent cells promote chronic inflammation, fibrosis, impaired regeneration, and metabolic dysfunction that contribute to SkM loss, SkM weakness, functional decline, and frailty. This review synthesizes current knowledge of the molecular drivers, hallmarks, and cellular origins of senescence within SkM and highlights the physiological consequences that extend from the cellular to the organismal level. We also discuss emerging senotherapeutic strategies that hold promise for optimizing SkM health and function with aging and disease.
n4a7543508958: The capacity to re-experience a moment from one's past, known as episodic memory, is critical for our ability to navigate the present and plan for the future. This article reviews and synthesizes over a half century of behavioral and neuroscientific research that has shaped our understanding of how we remember past events. This work has revealed complementary truths about episodic memory: Episodic memories seem to be based on traces of experience, carrying objective information about specific moments in time, and on imaginative reconstructions, built on a scaffold of prior knowledge. We propose that the tension between these perspectives can be reconciled by conceptualizing episodic memory not as a readout from a static memory system but as the outcome of two neurocognitive modes— a generative mode that facilitates schema-based inference and prediction, and a contextual mode that binds memories to context-specific anchor points. Drawing from experimental findings and computational models, we describe how multiple memory modes arise from dynamic cortico-hippocampal interactions, allowing episodic memory to be at once precise and constructive.
nf0f6e9d46b44: Introduction Movement behaviours (sleep, sedentary behaviour, and physical activity) influence numerous health outcomes in children, including their social-emotional development. The optimal 24-hour movement behaviour composition for positive social-emotional development is unknown. The purpose of this study was to determine the movement behaviour composition across the 24-hour day associated with desired social-emotional functioning in the early years. Methods This cross-sectional analysis included 560 children aged 1.2–2.9 years and 1,500 children aged 3.0–4.9 years from the Sleep and Activity Database (SADEY) for the Early Years study. Sedentary behaviour (SED), light physical activity (LPA), and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) were measured using ActiGraph accelerometers. Sleep duration was assessed using parent reports. Children social-emotional functioning was measured using the five domains of the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ), a widely used screening instrument of children’s behaviours, emotions, and relationships across five domains (emotional problems, conduct problems, hyperactivity, peer problems, and prosocial behaviour). Compositional data analyses were used to estimate the 24-hour movement behaviour compositions associated with optimal scores for each of the SDQ domain z-scores and all five domains combined (the Goldilocks day). Results The movement behaviour composition was significantly associated with all five SDQ domains (all p < .01). For 1–2-year-olds, the Goldilocks day consisted of 12 h 12 min of sleep, 4 h 36 min of SED, 5 h 48 min of LPA, and 1h 24 min of MVPA. For 3–4-year-olds, it consisted of 12 h 08 min of sleep, 4 h 27 min of SED, 5 h 49 min of LPA, and 1 h 36 min of MVPA. Conclusion The duration of total physical activity and MVPA associated with more favourable social-emotional functioning exceeded the minimum levels specified in the current 24-hour Movement Guidelines. These findings should not be interpreted as behavioural recommendations but rather as movement behaviour patterns associated with more favourable outcomes within this study population.
nd26bee347ee3: Researchers have long studied allostatic (over)load as an estimated measure of individual cumulative stress over a lifetime. Often called the overall ‘wear and tear’ from social and environmental stressors, allostatic (over)load shows promise as a practical indicator of general health trends in community settings. This data processing workflow aims to document our overall approach and reasoning when calculating allostatic (over)load for data analysis and knowledge sharing. The included repository features an R script for generating datasets using this workflow from the following data sources: All of Us Research Program data repository. Health and Retirement Study (HRS). National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). Our allostatic (over)load measurement process, along with the linked repository, provides a reproducible workflow to process secondary data and offers insights into protocol-driven measurement practices in community environments.
n6492c8cf0839: Aiming to balance localization accuracy, computational complexity, and robustness under low-SNR conditions in three-dimensional interference source localization, this paper proposes an efficient method combining frequency-domain covariance matrix reconstruction (FDCMR) and adaptive voxel iteration. First, the proposed method employs FDCMR-based direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for multi-station coarse localization and uses the intersection of direction cones to substantially compress the global search region. An adaptive voxel iteration with exponentially decreasing resolution is then performed within the compressed region for position refinement. Complexity analysis shows that the proposed method replaces exhaustive direct position determination (DPD) evaluation over the global search region with a bounded number of evaluations in a local adaptive voxel region, thereby substantially reducing the spatial-search complexity. Under the considered 2000 m × 2000 m × 2000 m search region with a 5 m spatial resolution, the number of DPD objective-function evaluations is reduced by approximately five orders of magnitude compared with conventional global DPD, while a localization accuracy of about 5 m is maintained at an SNR of 20 dB. At an SNR of −15 dB, the localization error is reduced by approximately 70% compared with the fixed-grid DPD method. These results demonstrate that the proposed method provides an effective balance between localization accuracy, computational efficiency, and low-SNR robustness.
n1d2b7014e8ab: The Artificial Potential Field (APF) method is widely used in robot path planning due to its simplicity and computational efficiency. However, it is well known to suffer from the local minima problem, where the resultant force acting on the robot becomes zero at non-goal configurations, leading to motion stagnation in cluttered environments. This paper proposes an optimization-based waypoint generation framework to address the local minima issue in APF navigation while ensuring explicit collision avoidance. When the direct path between the robot and the target is infeasible due to obstacle interference, intermediate waypoints are generated by solving a constrained optimization problem that guides the robot along a locally defined reference direction while enforcing obstacle clearance constraints for each path segment. Unlike conventional APF modifications that rely on artificial perturbation forces or random escape strategies, the proposed method constructs collision-free intermediate waypoints through finite candidate evaluation and explicit segment-wise collision checking, enabling the robot to avoid obstacles and overcome local-minima while preserving goal-directed motion and ensuring convergence to the target. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through numerical simulations on two robotic platforms, namely a point-mass robot and a wheelchair-type robotic model. The results demonstrate that the method successfully resolves local minima situations, ensures collision-free motion, and consistently guides the robots to their target locations in complex environments. Furthermore, the framework is general and can be applied to different robotic systems.
neb2692231f9d: by Md. Nuruzzaman Khan Background Reproductive coercion is an under-recognised form of violence against women and is not routinely captured by standard measures of intimate partner violence, which commonly focus on physical, sexual, and emotional violence. This study examined the association between reproductive coercion and these measured forms of intimate partner violence and estimated the proportion of women who reported reproductive coercion without reporting any of the physical, sexual, or emotional violence items included in the survey. Methods We analysed nationally representative data from 24,951 ever-married women, including 22,161 currently married women, in the Bangladesh Violence Against Women Survey 2024. Outcomes were physical, sexual, emotional, and any conventional IPV, assessed in the past 12 months among currently married women and over the lifetime among ever-married women. Exposures were reproductive coercion pattern and contraceptive coercion typology. Survey-weighted Poisson regression with robust standard errors estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) with 95% CIs for associations with conventional IPV. Survey-weighted logistic regression examined factors associated with reproductive coercion without reported conventional IPV and was considered exploratory because of the small number of events. Survey-weighted prevalence estimates were applied to 2022 census population counts to derive population estimates with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). Findings In the past 12 months, 27.30% of currently married women reported conventional IPV and 3.59% reported reproductive coercion; corresponding lifetime prevalences among ever-married women were 60.40% and 9.25%. Including reproductive coercion increased the prevalence of any reported abuse to 28.61% and 61.18%, respectively. Reproductive coercion was associated with a higher prevalence of each form of conventional IPV, with the largest aPRs among women reporting multiple forms of reproductive coercion. Reproductive coercion without reported conventional IPV was reported by 1.31% (95% CI 1.08–1.59) of currently married women in the past 12 months and 0.78% (0.60–1.01) of ever-married women over the lifetime, corresponding to approximately 645,483 (95% UI 532,154–783,449) and 437,414 (337,106–567,462) women, respectively. Interpretation Reproductive coercion captures a dimension of violence against women that is only partly reflected in conventional IPV measures. Women reporting reproductive coercion without conventional IPV might have experienced unmeasured or unreported violence; therefore, this group indicates a measurement gap rather than absence of other abuse. Including validated reproductive coercion measures in national violence surveys could improve evidence for health, legal, and social support responses.
nd0e5411458ab: Introduction Long COVID is a complex pathophysiological condition linked to a heterogenous symptom profile. Dysregulation of 1) immunological and inflammatory responses, 2) endothelial/vascular function, and 3) metabolic and clotting processes have been identified; however, there remains a lack of clinically validated diagnostic biomarkers. The study aim was to investigate dysregulation of cytokines, chemokines and growth factors in confirmed Long COVID cases grouped by disease severity. Methods One-hundred-and-twenty-seven participants provided venous blood samples for cytokine profiling utilising Luminex assays. Participants were grouped into those with no knowledge of SARS-CoV-2 infection (n = 21), acute infection within 3-months (n = 22), spontaneous resolvers (>3-months, n = 21) and those with confirmed Long COVID (n = 63). Long COVID severity was grouped according to the post-COVID-19 functional status (PCFS) and defined as those with negligible (4A; n = 9), mild (4B; n = 20), moderate (4C; n = 24), and severe limitations (4D; n = 10). Cytokines were assessed for normality using Shapiro-Wilk tests and differences measured between groups using Kruskal-Wallis tests. Pairwise correlation and principal component analysis were performed. Results Interleukin-12 (p40/p70) was 22% greater in the Long COVID group (Median [IQR]: 58 [49] pg/mL, p = 0.046) and 30% greater in the acutely infected group (64 [36] pg/mL; p = 0.039) against non-infected controls (45 [25] pg/mL). Following PCFS classification, fibroblast growth factor-basic was 25% lower in Long COVID 4B versus spontaneous resolvers (24 [7] vs. 32 [24] pg/mL; p = 0.025). Pairwise correlation differences demonstrated that three Long COVID subgroups had strong, positive associations between cytokines when compared to non-infected controls; however, PCA was unable to determine any coordinated cytokine variation that was group specific. Discussion and conclusions Elevated interleukin-12 (p40/p70) and reduced basic fibroblast growth factor suggest persistent immune activation and possible subgroup-specific Long COVID; however, these findings were marginally significant and exploratory. A coordinated but partial immunological/inflammatory profile may exist in some of those with Long COVID, suggesting a rationale for subgrouping upon a biological, rather than self-report basis but larger longitudinal studies are required to confirm this hypothesis.
